s.t: The Sr Product Owner plays a critical role in ensuring that a product or feature is developed with a focus on delivering value to the customer and the business. They act as a voice for the customer and are responsible for making key product-related decisions throughout the development process, including identifying opportunities to incorporate emerging technologies, such as AI-enabled capabilities, where they can improve user experience, workflow efficiency, and business outcomes.

Product Vision & Stakeholder Alignment
Translation: Work with stakeholders to translate future vision and requirements into clearly broken-down epics and stories; ensure all team members understand and align with product goals, including consideration of emerging technologies where appropriate.
Stakeholder Communication: Act as the primary point of contact between the development team and stakeholders; communicate progress, changes, and updates regularly.
Team Enabler: Work with one or more Agile Development Teams and act as a central reference and information source, guiding system/product functionality decisions.
Entrepreneurial Spirit: Demonstrate a track record of delivering results in fast-moving, demanding environments.
Backlog Ownership & Prioritization
Prioritization: Create and maintain the product backlog; prioritize features, user stories, and tasks based on business value, customer needs, market trends, and strategic opportunities.
Backlog Management: Continuously groom and refine the backlog based on feedback, changing priorities, and new insights.
Feedback Integration: Gather and incorporate feedback from stakeholders and end-users into the backlog; adjust as necessary.

User Story Development: Break down high-level requirements into detailed, implementable user stories that meet strong Agile standards and support effective workflows, automation, and decision support where applicable.
Acceptance Criteria: Define clear acceptance criteria so the team understands what constitutes “done” for each feature.
UI/UX Alignment: Partner with UX to ensure backlog items have wireframes and UI designs ready for sprint planning; provide design feedback, participate in design sprints, and support user acceptance testing.
Planning, Delivery & Risk
Sprint Planning: Participate in sprint planning to select stories and tasks; ensure the team has a clear understanding of work scope.
Release Planning: Collaborate with the team and stakeholders to plan and prioritize releases aligned with market needs and business goals.
Quality Assurance: Ensure the product meets quality standards by accepting or rejecting work during sprint reviews.
Risk Management: Identify and mitigate delivery risks; partner with the release manager on timelines, tough conversations, mitigation strategies, and transparent escalation to leadership.
Business Outcomes & Data
Business Case Support: Assist in developing and presenting business cases for new features and initiatives; ensure alignment with strategic goals and stakeholder expectations.
Data-Driven: Define KPIs and measures for features and capabilities to track impact and inform decisions.

Our mission is to make education financing more accessible and engaging, while giving brands a way to connect with the next generation.
We’re powered by AI technology that simplifies scholarship discovery, streamlines the application process, and delivers measurable results for both students and partners. Whether it’s helping students secure funding or enabling brands to run impactful campaigns, we’re reshaping how education is funded — and discovered.

We’re looking for a Growth Product Manager to take full ownership of the conversion engine at ScholarshipOwl, from the first visitor touchpoint through to a paid subscription. This is a high-impact, high-velocity role for someone who lives in the data, thrives on experimentation, and values action over perfection.
You will be the architect of our growth. You’ll spend your days identifying leaks in the funnel, hypothesizing solutions, and working alongside a dedicated pod of engineers and designers to ship experiments that move the needle on revenue and retention. If you are a "full-stack" growth thinker who can move from a Mixpanel cohort analysis to a detailed technical spec this is the role for you.

Own the Conversion Engine: Take end-to-end responsibility for the user journey, optimizing every step from landing page registration to paywall conversion and subscription retention.
Drive the Experiment Roadmap: Build, prioritize, and maintain a high-tempo experimentation backlog. You will use frameworks (like ICE or RICE) to ensure we are always working on the highest-leverage growth bets.
Analyze & Diagnose: Monitor funnel and retention metrics daily in Mixpanel. You’ll identify exactly where users are dropping off and perform deep-dive discovery to understand the why .
Ship with Velocity: Write precise product specs and acceptance criteria that allow engineering and design to execute independently. We prioritize shipping "good enough" tests today to get data, rather than waiting for "perfect" features next month.
Optimize Revenue Levers: Design and run pricing, paywall, and offer optimization tests. You’ll also evaluate new growth levers like organic loops, landing page personalization, and winback programs.
Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Lead a dedicated pod of engineers and designers, maintaining strong working relationships with our dashboard and B2B teams to drive unified sprint priorities.
Continuous Discovery: Conduct meaningful customer discovery interviews with our Gen-Z audience to uncover behavioral insights that data alone can’t show.

5+ years of Product Management experience , specifically in a Growth -focused role.
Experimentation Mastery: Proven track record of designing, running, and analyzing A/B tests that resulted in measurable improvements to business KPIs (CVR, ARPU, Churn).
Data Fluency: You are a power user of product analytics tools (Mixpanel, Amplitude, or similar). You don't wait for a data analyst; you find the answers yourself.
SaaS/Subscription Expertise: You understand the nuances of subscription models—trial-to-paid transitions, renewal cycles, and friction-point reduction.
Technical Precision: Ability to write clear, "dev-ready" product specs and acceptance criteria. You understand technical trade-offs and how to scope an MVP.
Mentoring & Leadership: A mentoring and knowledge-sharing mindset with a desire to level up the broader team on growth methodologies and experimentation rigor.
Gen-Z Empathy: You have an intuition for (or experience with) B2C products targeting younger audiences and understand their unique digital behaviors.
Growth Mindset: You are comfortable with ambiguity, fast-moving environments, and the fact that 70% of experiments might fail—as long as we learn from them.

We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.
We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

Product Manager: Alternative Payment Processing
Checkout.com is seeking a Product Manager and leader to join our team of product managers working to add and improve our Alternative Payment Method (APM) portfolio, with a focus on bank-based payment rails.

This role will help drive our company OKR of expanding and enhancing the payment methods we offer merchants around the world, helping these businesses grow their global footprint.

The successful candidate will provide cross-functional leadership across product, engineering, and business teams, to ensure our APM portfolio is embedded throughout Checkout.com ’s ecosystem, enabling a seamless experience for our merchants.

They will work across the business and engage with merchants to align on the selection of APMs, drive the recommended approach to offer or improve them, design the API experience and collaborate with more than twenty stakeholder teams to deliver APMs end-to-end.

Daily tasks include understanding stakeholders’ pain points, driving prioritization for product development, and developing new capabilities for our customers.

3-5 years of product management experience.
Experience working in payment methods, especially direct debit and account-to-account payment methods
Data-driven: Skilled at leveraging data and business insights to determine strategic priorities and drive the product roadmap and execution.
Customer-first: Think from the customer's perspective and can balance future opportunities with immediate needs.
End-to-end mindset: Think in a structured and diligent manner, understanding all key components necessary to drive the ongoing success of a product.
Leadership: Excellent at collaborating with stakeholders in product, engineering, commercial, and business teams proactively, demonstrating high EQ and influencing skills.
Effective communicator: Able to inspire others with a shared vision and simplify complex concepts for a wide range of audiences.

Set the strategy for your portfolio of APMs, including understanding the target market, customers and aims for each APM, to determine the best approach for delivering the APMs, and how to balance adding new APMs vs working on enhancements for the existing portfolio, using qualitative and quantitative research and data to make decisions.
Become an expert in your payment methods, working closely with the payment partners to understand trends and drivers for success, which you will leverage to support our commercial team and drive value for our merchants.
Work with engineering and product counterparts to design the API and integration for each APM, to deliver an optimal developer experience which balances a consistent API experience across Checkout.com ’s products with the nuances of each different APM.
Build strong partnerships with business, product, and technology stakeholders and work with them for their buy-in and collaboration to generate momentum for your products
Work with other product and engineering leaders to ensure alignment with their roadmaps and delivery
Gain a deep understanding of Checkout.com ’s customers and business.
Foster a team culture that upholds Checkout.com ’s operating principles.

Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast.

Deltakit is Riverlane’s open-source software development kit (SDK) for QEC which is designed to help researchers build, test and run QEC workflows as the field of quantum computing rapidly evolves.

Beyond the roadmap, you’ll play a key role in bringing Deltakit to life for the community. From supporting launches to engaging directly with users, you’ll shape how we show up, tell our story, and communicate the product’s value in a way that excites and inspires people to build with it.

Maintain a backlog of well-defined and prioritized user stories that align with customer needs and business goals.
Minimize scope changes and rework through effective communication and requirement validation.
Stakeholder Alignment : Establish strong communication channels with stakeholders and ensure a shared understanding of product vision, progress, and timelines. This includes:
Build and maintain trust-based relationships with stakeholders by providing clear, structured, and consistent communication.
Proactively address stakeholder concerns and manage expectations to ensure alignment with the product roadmap.
Data-informed decisions : Drive continuous improvement of the product through data analysis, user feedback, and iterative development cycles. This includes:
Monitor and analyze key product and team KPIs (e.g., conversion rates, user engagement) to identify opportunities for enhancement.
Utilize data insights to prioritize features and improvements that have the highest impact on user satisfaction and business goals.
Implement iterative development practices, adjusting priorities and features based on real-time feedback and changing market conditions.

We are mainly looking for this role based in Germany, preferably at our headquarters in Berlin. We are a remote-first company, with teams around the Globe and our HQ office in Berlin, where the team often meets in the office.

At least 3+ years of professional experience as a Product Owner
Have user-centric thinking: Ability to empathize with users, understand their needs, and prioritize features based on their value and impact
Strong communicator: You possess verbal and written communication skills to effectively convey the product vision, requirements, and updates to both the development team and stakeholders
Know Agile Methodology: You are proficient in Agile methodologies (particularly Scrum) to manage iterative development, prioritize work, and respond to changing requirements.
Hands-on with user story writing: You are able to break down complex features into clear and concise user stories that capture user needs, acceptance criteria, and business value.
Technically savvy: You understand the technical aspects of the product domain, allowing effective translation of requirements into actionable tasks for the development team.
Data-driven decision mindset: Your skills in using data and analytics help you make informed decisions, monitor KPIs, and identify areas for product improvement.
Problem-Solving approach: You are able to identify and address challenges that arise during product development, find creative solutions, and make timely adjustments.
Adaptability: You are willing to embrace change and adapt to evolving user needs, market trends, and business priorities
Experience with B2C products is a plus.

You will join a fast-paced travel tech company and take on a rapidly growing industry
You will take on ownership and responsibility from day one and have a direct impact on the success of the company
We value agility! We’re constantly updating our tech stack and offer the best possible tools to ensure all of our in-house engineers, partners, and carriers benefit from cutting-edge, efficient solutions.
You will work with global companies. Our product attracts the biggest names in travel technology, such as Booking.com, and Google Maps, and national carriers like Amtrak, Deutsche Bahn, Renfe, and SNCF.
You will join an international team of talented and driven people with a clear mission. Expect your colleagues to inspire, support, and challenge you every day!
We offer flexible and remote working conditions, relocation opportunities, and career growth in a small and developing company

At Google, we put our users first. The world is always changing, so we need Product Managers who are continuously adapting and excited to work on products that affect millions of people every day.
In this role, you will work cross-functionally to guide products from conception to launch by connecting the technical and business worlds. You can break down complex problems into steps that drive product development.
One of the many reasons Google consistently brings innovative, world-changing products to market is because of the collaborative work we do in Product Management. Our team works closely with creative engineers, designers, marketers, etc. to help design and develop technologies that improve access to the world's information.

We're responsible for guiding products throughout the execution cycle, focusing specifically on analyzing, positioning, packaging, promoting, and tailoring our solutions to our users.
The Ads in AI Experiences team is responsible for one of the highest-priority initiatives at Google: reinventing Search Ads for the AI era (AI Overview, AI Mode). We are building the tech stack, the user experience, and the business model simultaneously.

Our mission is to ensure that as Search experience evolves with AI, we unlock new ways for users to discover and engage with businesses through seamless, next-generation commercial experiences. We are a team of risk-takers and builders, responsible for experimenting with rapid velocity to define the next decade of Google-s revenue engine.
Google Ads is helping power the open internet with the best technology that connects and creates value for people, publishers, advertisers, and Google. We-re made up of multiple teams, building Google-s Advertising products including search, display, shopping, travel and video advertising, as well as analytics.

Our teams create trusted experiences between people and businesses with useful ads. We help grow businesses of all sizes from small businesses, to large brands, to YouTube creators, with effective advertiser tools that deliver measurable results. We also enable Google to engage with customers at scale.

* Re-invent Search ads for these new AI experiences - AI Mode and AI Overviews (AIX2). Experiment with a wide variety of new Ad experiences in AI Experiences and launch the subset of these that are successful.

Über Patronus
Patronus entwickelt intelligente Notruf-Technologie, die Senior*innen mehr Sicherheit und Unabhängigkeit im Alltag gibt. Mehr als 25.000 Menschen verlassen sich bereits auf uns. Als Berliner Healthcare Start-up mit finanzstarken Investoren im Rücken wachsen wir schnell – und genau dieses Wachstum treibst du in deiner Rolle aktiv mit voran.
Als Senior Product Manager Mobile ( w/m/x ) wirst du Teil unseres Product-Management-Teams und berichtest direkt an den Team Lead Product Management. Du übernimmst die operative Produktverantwortung für iOS, Android und unsere Smartwatch-App . Du entwickelst die Mobile Experience gemeinsam mit Engineering, QA und den relevanten Stakeholdern weiter. Was uns als Team ausmacht: schnelle Iterationen , viel Eigenverantwortung und konsequente Nutzerorientierung .
Deine Mission
Produktverantwortung Mobile: Vollständige Ownership für iOS, Android und Smartwatch-App inkl. Roadmap.
Discovery & Anforderungen: Nutzerforschung und Kundengespräche in User Stories und priorisiertes Backlog übersetzen.
Datengetriebene Entscheidungen: User Behavior, KPIs und Nutzerfeedback analysieren, Hypothesen ableiten und validieren.
Growth & Retention: Denken in DAU/MAU, Retention, Churn, Aktivierung. A/B-Testing als Wachstumstreiber.
Prozesse & UX: Durchdachte Workflows und herausragende Mobile-Experience auf drei Plattformen.
Qualität & Support: Hands-on Feature Testing, QA-Begleitung, AI Prototyping und UI-Generierung sowie Unterstützung des Customer Supports.
Dein Talent
Mind. 5 Jahre Erfahrung als Product Manager mit Fokus auf Mobile-Anwendungen (iOS, Android, Smartwatch)
Erfahrung in dynamischen Unternehmen mit schneller Umsetzung, wechselnden Anforderungen und echtem Gestaltungsspielraum
Nachweislich datengetriebene Arbeitsweise mit App-KPIs, Nutzerfeedback und Analytics als Grundlage
Exzellentes Stakeholder-Management & Hands-on Mentaltität
Erfahrung mit UX-/UI-Design (Figma) und Prototyping
Offenheit für AI und idealerweise Erfahrung mit Hotjar, Miro, Mixpanel und Jira
Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse, jeweils mindestens auf C1-Niveau

⚖️ Fair von Anfang an : Du bekommst von uns direkt unser bestmögliches Angebot – wir gehen von Anfang an mit der Zahl rein, die woanders erst am Ende einer Verhandlung steht.
🏢 Arbeitsort : 2 Tage pro Woche mobil arbeiten sowie klimatisiertes Büro mit Spree-Blick mitten in Friedrichshain
📚 Wachstum : 500€ jährliches Learning & Development-Budget, klarer Career Framework und 360°-Feedback für deine Weiterentwicklung
🤝 Miteinander : Wir feiern Erfolge gemeinsam bei regelmäßigen Company Events und bei vierteljährlichen Teamevents mit 50€ Budget pro Person für besondere Erlebnisse (z.B. Escape Rooms, Cooking Classes oder Game Shows)
🏖️ Urlaub : Bis zu 30 Tage Urlaub (nach Start mit 26 im 1. & 28 im 2. Jahr)
🧘 Fitness & Freizeit : Bis zu 50% Rabatt auf Urban Sports Club, Corporate Benefits, Restaurant-Deals sowie Family & Friends Coupon auf die Patronus Uhr
🚲 Mobilität : 30% Rabatt aufs Job Ticket sowie vergünstigtes Fahrrad-Leasing
🥤 Verpflegung : Kostenfreie Softdrinks & Kaffeevollautomat, Müslibar, vierteljährliche Company Brunches sowie wöchentliche Healthy Snacks
💻 Hardware : Freie Wahl zwischen MacBook und Lenovo
🌍 Impact : Ein Produkt mit echtem gesellschaftlichem Mehrwert plus ein Volunteering-Tag im Jahr
Einfach. Sicher. Leben. Mit Patronus.
Wir sind mehr als ein Anbieter für intelligente Notruf-Uhren – wir entwickeln Technologien, die Menschen ein selbstbestimmtes Leben ermöglichen: We create a world where aging is delightful.
Möglich macht das unsere revolutionäre Patronus-Uhr: Auf den ersten Blick nicht als Notruf erkennbar, ermöglicht sie es Nutzer*innen, jederzeit und überall unkompliziert Hilfe zu rufen. Damit sorgen wir für Sicherheit und retten im wahrsten Sinne des Wortes Leben.

Sie ist dabei unser Türöffner, um das Leben älterer Menschen, ihrer Angehörigen und Pflegepersonen zu verbessern und das Gesundheitssystem effektiver zu machen. Damit in Zukunft alle Menschen ihr Leben so leben können, wie sie es möchten.
Klingt nach einer perfekten Stelle für dich?
Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung und darauf, dich kennenzulernen!
Auch wenn du unserem Anforderungsprofil nicht zu 100 % entsprichst, ermutigen wir dich trotzdem, dich bei uns zu bewerben.
Patronus ist ein Arbeitgeber, der Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt fördert. Wir bemühen uns, ein freundliches, sicheres und einladendes Umfeld für alle unsere Mitarbeiter*innen zu schaffen, unabhängig von ethnischer Herkunft, Geschlecht, Geschlechtsidentität und -ausdruck, sexueller Orientierung, Einschränkungen und Begabungen jeglicher Art, körperlicher Erscheinung, sozialem Hintergrund, Familienstand, Alter oder Religion (oder deren Fehlen).

Habitat Health empowers older adults to experience more good days in their homes and communities. Through the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE), we provide comprehensive medical care along with support for daily needs such as meals, transportation, and in‑home assistance.

We deliver coordinated clinical and social care in our centers and directly in participants’ homes, creating a fully integrated experience that brings peace of mind and a true sense of belonging.

As we expand our scalable, affordable PACE model to meet the growing and complex needs of aging populations, our mission‑driven care teams continue to help participants live well on their own terms.
Habitat Health is supported by leading healthcare organizations and investors including New Enterprise Associates, Kaiser Permanente, and Town Hall Ventures. We are entering a period of significant growth and are looking for exceptional teammates to help us scale a better model of care for older adults. To learn more, visit www.habitathealth.com.
Role Scope
Habitat Health is hiring its first Data Product Manager to report to the VP of Product. We are looking for a generalist, hands-on, highly technical individual contributor who will own the roadmap for Habitat's data products and infrastructure, setting direction and priorities across the data function. You will own data products end-to-end across the two major Habitat Health pillars that the data team supports:
Platform & Integrations , including Engineering / IT / Product / Technical & AI vendors
Dashboards & Reporting , across growth, clinical, financial, and administrative data sets
In this role you will serve as the key bridge between our Product and Data functions, working closely with C-Suite and VP level stakeholders to align on the right product strategy, then rolling up your sleeves and collaborating with our development team to build data products that align with business needs. To succeed as a Data PM, you will need to balance Habitat’s high level business objectives against end user needs and development constraints.
In a given week you'll move across all of the modes below: figuring out what's actually worth building (Discovery), writing specs precise enough for developers to build from without back-and-forth (Specs), running the Jira backlog and sprint process (Delivery), keeping development unblocked (Execution management), mocking up and shipping dashboards (Design, QC, UAT), and triaging the daily stream of ad hoc requests from a diverse set of data customers (Triage).

s.h: Core Responsibilities & Expectations for the Role
s.t:
Discovery : define the business problem before the build (e.g. is automating LOPMR for CMS audits the right priority this quarter?).
Build and ship : own the full delivery cycle – specs, Jira/sprint process, dashboard design and sign-off, UAT, and rollout.
Hands-on data work : use SQL and Git to independently query, validate, and review code, not just manage a backlog.
Triage : distinguish quick fixes from roadmap work across a steady stream of ad hoc requests.
AI fluency : use AI tools (e.g. Claude) to accelerate the work and model that fluency for the team.
Range : move across all Platform & Integrations, Clinical & Operational Services, Regulatory and Enterprise Reporting, helping shape how data product works at Habitat.

3 to 5+ years of experience in product management, data/BI, or a closely related field, with a track record of shipping data products, dashboards, or reporting tools end-to-end (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
Solid understanding of healthcare data ontologies, systems, and information technology
Proficiency in SQL sufficient to independently query, validate, and troubleshoot data.
Demonstrated ability to write clear technical specs (metric definitions, cohort logic, source-to-target mapping ,etc.)
Experience partnering directly with business stakeholders and end users – e.g., operations, compliance, or clinical leadership – to gather requirements, design solutions, and lead user acceptance testing.
Familiarity with a modern data development stack (e.g., Jira, Git, Power BI, and cloud data platforms such as Databricks or Azure) sufficient to spec, review, and troubleshoot alongside engineering.
Comfort and enthusiasm using AI tools to enhance productivity in requirements writing, documentation, analysis, and workflow automation.
Aligns with our purpose and our values, and is excited about living those out in daily practice
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment with comfort navigating ambiguity, adapting quickly, and contributing to continuous improvement
Strong learning and growth mindset, including seeking feedback, engaging in healthy debate and using data and curiosity to inform decisions.
Acts with integrity and ownership, considering the broader organizational impact, doing the right thing, and following through to deliver results.

Working knowledge of Agile/Scrum practices, including backlog grooming, sprint planning, and Jira (or similar tools).
Experience in PACE, VBC, or another regulated, compliance-driven environment, including deep working knowledge of healthcare data ontologies (e.g., CPT, ICD-10, NDC).
Experience with Epic (Clarity, Caboodle, Chronicles), medical/pharmacy claims data, or FHIR/HL7-based integrations.

The Brecknell Scales Global Product Manager owns the full product lifecycle and global strategy for the Brecknell Scales portfolio ( with additional Salter and AWTX branded products ). This is a hands-on role that blends strategic product management with technical sales support and supplier relationship management.
Brecknell focuses on affordable, easy-to-use, competitively priced scales primarily sourced from China (approx. 80% of volume). Key markets include medical, veterinary, food service/POS, postal/mail/shipping, and sports fishing.

The role drives revenue growth, maintains strong margins where possible through unique/owned designs, mitigates risks from market saturation and direct-from-China competition, and ensures products remain simple, compliant, and low-maintenance to minimize technical support calls.

Own the end-to-end product lifecycle for the entire Brecknell Scales portfolio — from new product discovery and market validation through launch, growth, maturity, and obsolescence/end-of-life planning.
Conduct regular product health checks and market analysis per key sector (medical, vet, food service, postal, etc.) to identify gaps, growth opportunities, and missing product needs.
Translate customer, sales, and market insights into clear product requirements, prioritized feature requests, and a multi-year global product roadmap.
Act as the primary voice of the customer and global market, ensuring Brecknell products remain simple to set up and use “out of the box” while reducing technical support needs.
Define and maintain product positioning, value propositions, and go-to-market strategies, with emphasis on globalization (harmonized SKUs across USA, UK, and ROW where possible).
Lead New Product Introduction (NPI) activities, targeting faster time-to-market (ideally 5–6 months), including pricing strategy, launch planning, sales enablement, training, brochures, manuals, datasheets, and website updates.
Manage supplier relationships with key Chinese partners, including price negotiations, quality improvements, lead time management, new product development, and proactive identification of next-generation suppliers to maintain cost competitiveness and quality.
Manage relationships with AWTX China, and AWTX India
Monitor and resolve obsolescence, component shortages, inventory/SMI/stockout issues, and quality holds in collaboration with purchasing, quality, and regional teams.
Ensure full regulatory compliance across regions (NTEP, OIML, NSF, FDA registration/listing, UPC-A/EAN-13 barcodes, safe battery shipping certificates, etc.) and manage associated annual fees/renewals.
Analyze product performance metrics (sales, margin, adoption, returns, warranty data, customer feedback) and conduct competitive analysis to drive improvements, portfolio rationalization, and margin protection on unique/owned products (e.g., Electrosamson, 6700U, ZP and Salter products).
Partner with marketing to keep all product documentation, images, quick-start guides (including French/Spanish), and sales tools up to date.
Interpret technical specifications, drawings, and datasheets, translating them into clear, customer-friendly language and supporting private labeling/OEM opportunities.
Drive initiatives for product enhancement to extend product lifecycle, keep products simple, easy to use and low-cost while adding smart features/benefits.
Support annual pricing reviews, price list updates (including Shopify/discontinued lists), and PLS/phase-out decisions.
Provide Technical support to customers and end users for the UK/RoW (NA tech support provided from Fairmont

Provide expert technical sales support for complex enquiries, RFQs, tenders, and end user customer applications across the Brecknell (Salter and AWTX ZP) range.

You'll own one of Letly's product surfaces end to end — the money surface (rent collection, deposits, landlord payouts, statements and the ledger underneath them) or the marketplace (AI-Native property management, the vendor network and the embedded products sold into a tenancy) — the product and the operation running on it.
We don't sell software to this industry, we run the industry ourselves: every product decision you make lands in a real tenancy, a real payment and a real operator's day, usually within the week.
These are mid-to-senior hires. At mid you own a surface and ship it. At senior you own a surface others depend on — you set the product patterns, take the architecture-shaped calls with engineering, and raise the bar around you.
What you'll own
The console the business runs on. The internal surface ops actually works in, whichever side you own. Every hour of manual work you design out is margin.

Rent in. Collection across thousands of tenancies — mandates, retries, part-payments and arrears — and the tenant-facing product wrapped around it.
Money out. Landlord payouts, statements, deposits and pooled client money: right to the penny, on the day we promised, compliant, and legible to a landlord who is not an accountant.
The ledger and reconciliation. A penny-accurate, self-healing ledger reconciling bank activity across every tenancy, plus the tooling ops reaches for when it doesn't match.
Money agents in production. Agents that chase arrears, answer "where is my rent", and escalate to a human. You decide what they're allowed to do, what the guardrails are, and where the handover sits.

AI-Native property management. The managed product itself — maintenance, compliance, renewals, inspections — run by agents with humans only on the exceptions, across the service ladder from self-managing to guaranteed.
The vendor network. Supply on the services side: contractors, engineers, cleaners, inventory clerks, photographers. Onboarding, pricing, SLAs, quality controls, and the routing that picks the right one without a human in the middle.
Embedded products. Insurance, compliance certificates, referencing and utilities sold into the tenancy at the moment they're needed — attach rate, take-rate and the unit economics of each.
The landlord and tenant journey. Listing → viewing → offer → referencing → contract → tenancy → renewal, built as one product across both sides of a transaction that has never been one product.
How we work
You get your own answers — query the data, read the tickets, sit with ops, do the job manually once before you specify it.
You use AI across your own work: research, specs, prototypes, analysis. We expect a PM to operate AI-Natively and run product operations.
Weekly release cadence, decisions written down, evidence over opinion.

3+ years owning product end to end in a high-growth environment (more, for senior), including at least one thing you launched from zero.
Technical range: you can intelligently discuss system design, APIs, data models and failure modes, and engineers respect your judgement.
You do your own analysis — you're comfortable in the data and you prioritise on expected impact, not on who asked.
Operational literacy: you can design a process and a product together, and you know which of the two is the right fix.
AI-Native: you use models expertly, and you can specify an agentic product — scope, guardrails, evals and failure modes included.
Depth in one of our two surfaces: either a payments, lending, insurance or banking product you owned — treating reconciliation, failure paths and regulatory constraints as product problems rather than edge cases — or supply or demand in a two-sided marketplace, with liquidity, matching, take-rate and the quality controls that keep both sides coming back.
Senior: a track record of owning a surface others depended on, and of raising the standard of the people around you.

Exposure to the other surface — money if you come from marketplaces, marketplaces if you come from money.
Property or lettings experience.
First PM into a company, or a technical degree / having shipped code yourself.
Who does well here
You own the number, not the roadmap — the roadmap is a means to it.
You go to the operation — the answer is in the property, the call recording and the ledger, not in the backlog.
You decide — with incomplete information, in writing, and you revisit when the evidence changes.
You compress — you'd rather delete a step than design a screen for it.
Why apply
Letly is the AI-Native operating company built for the home. We believe the home will be autonomously run by AI and we're building the software that will run all rental properties end-to-end, starting with London (the world's 2nd largest rental city).
You'll get to own the whole loop: build the software, run the operation on it, and watch the unit economics move. You own the output metric, not just the process. The domain is the largest financial relationship in most people's lives and for the first time in history, technology enables us to crack it. The surface you own will be one of the first parts of it to run itself.
We've raised a $4m pre-seed from investors who've built the financial and operational infrastructure that moves billions and serves millions. They backed us because the home is the largest consumer asset where that infrastructure hasn't been built yet. You'll get competitive base pay, meaningful equity, and a small, high-agency team rebuilding an industry and growing at >100% month-over-month. We're hiring to facilitate this aggressive growth.

Homebound is on a mission to make it possible for anyone, anywhere, to build a home using technology. Created by an experienced team of construction, real estate, design, and technology experts, Homebound is transforming the residential construction industry by improving the costly and inefficient process of building a home.
We’ve created an entirely new way to build homes with technology powering every stage from start to finish to provide a seamless experience for our customers. Homeowners across the country can choose where they want to live, select a home plan that’s perfect for them, then personalize and buy it, all online.

Homebound has raised $150M in capital from leading venture capitalists like Google, Khosla, Thrive Ventures, and we’re scaling quickly in places like Texas, Colorado and Florida. Come build your future with us.

As Senior Product Manager - Field AI, you will own the forward-looking technology that brings AI to the teams building our homes. This is where the physical and digital worlds meet: your users are the Superintendents and Direct Construction Operators (DCOs) on the jobsite, and your product surface spans our mobile application, advanced onsite AI tools, automated data capture, and probabilistic construction schedules with insight analysis.
This is a role for a thought leader in applied AI. We are looking for someone with a strong point of view on how emerging technologies - computer vision, agents, LLMs, and multimodal models - can be applied in a physical, unstructured environment to make our field teams faster, more accurate, and more effective.

You don't need a construction background (though genuine curiosity about the built world is a plus), but you do need real experience translating frontier AI into products that work in the real world, outside the browser.
You'll own the roadmap, execution, and success metrics for the field AI portfolio, and you'll operate as an independent, cross-functional force connecting Construction Operations, Field Operations, and Engineering.

Own the field AI strategy and roadmap: Set the vision and execute end-to-end across the entirety of our field portfolio - from concept to rollout.
Bring AI into the physical environment: Translate the capabilities of computer vision, multimodal models, and agents into products that operate reliably on an active jobsite, where inputs are messy and conditions change daily.
Lead as a thought partner: Bring a strong, well-formed perspective on where field technology is going, and use it to shape how Homebound applies new technologies to the teams building our homes.
Embed with the field: Travel to Texas monthly to work directly with Superintendents and DCOs, run trainings, drive rollouts, and build the tight feedback loops that make field products actually stick.
Drive progress across teams: Operate independently and move initiatives forward across Construction Operations, Operations, and Engineering without waiting for a playbook.
Define product with rigor: Write clear, actionable requirements, establish evaluation and quality frameworks for AI features, and prioritize based on impact, effort, and long-term value.
Measure what matters: Define success metrics and run experiments to systematically improve accuracy, adoption, and field efficiency.

5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of a complex, technical product.
A track record of shipping applied AI products - computer vision, multimodal, LLM/agent-based, or ML systems - that took meaningful action or made decisions in production, not just chat wrappers or lightweight integrations.
Demonstrated experience applying technology in the physical world or in traditionally non-tech, unstructured environments (a strong plus).
Strong technical fluency - comfortable operating alongside engineers and ML teams as peers, reasoning through system tradeoffs, reading evaluations, and diving into the data to answer your own questions.
A self-starter and independent operator who thrives in ambiguity, moves quickly, and drives outcomes cross-functionally without heavy process.
A genuine thought leader in emerging AI - you follow the frontier closely and have a point of view on how to apply it.
0→1 product building: hands-on experience taking a product from concept through launch to real-world adoption.
Exceptional communication skills and the ability to translate seamlessly between field needs, technical teams, and executive leadership.
Willingness to travel to Texas monthly to work shoulder-to-shoulder with our field teams.
Interest in construction and the built environment is a plus; no prior industry experience required, but an expectation to learn the domain rapidly.

Now, we’re scaling fast and building the next generation of products to accelerate the green energy transition.

From making it effortless to switch to heat pumps, solar and EVs, to launching smart tariffs and creating renewable generation at scale, we’re solving some of the most complex challenges in energy with speed, creativity and customer obsession.

We’re also enabling our global businesses to reach the full capability of what we’ve achieved in the UK, taking the learnings, products and experiences that customers love here and rolling them out worldwide.

Our mobile app is how millions of customers interact with Octopus every day. It's global first, lives across multiple countries, and is growing fast.We need a Product Manager who can own the product direction for key areas of the app, navigate a complex stakeholder landscape, and ship features that genuinely make customers' lives easier.
This is a role where you’ll be fully embedded with engineers and designers, shaping what we build and how we build it. You'll coordinate across country teams, balancing local needs with a global product vision. And you'll do it at startup pace, because even though we're big now, we still move like we're small.
At Octopus Tech, you'll have real ownership, variety, and the chance to shape products that make a tangible difference in people's lives: lowering bills, enabling greener living, and delivering experiences customers genuinely love. You'll work side by side with teams across marketing, operations, and data, and see the impact of your work in the real world, fast.
What you’ll be doing…
Owning the product roadmap for your area of the mobile app, setting direction and making the calls on what gets built and when.
Coordinating across Octopus's global markets. Our app serves customers in multiple countries, so you'll navigate competing priorities, align stakeholders, and find the right balance between local needs and global consistency.
Working closely with engineers, designers, and data teams to define problems, shape solutions, and ship iteratively.
Defining technical requirements for dependencies on other teams and clearly communicating priority to external teams.
Developing, testing, and releasing features with scalability in mind.
Scoping larger underlying system changes and making pragmatic decisions about sequencing.
Monitoring existing customer journeys and new releases, using data to drive decisions and catch issues early.
Collaborating with local Operations teams to test changes and debug issues with live journeys.
Regular touchpoints with Marketing to identify trends, issues or improvements across funnels.
Working across multiple teams (Marketing, Ops, Credit, Design, country leads) to build shared understanding and drive alignment.
What you'll have...
3+ years of product management experience, with meaningful time spent working on mobile apps.
Experience in startups or fast-moving scale-ups where you've had to figure things out without a rigid playbook.
A track record of shipping mobile products that real people use and love.
The ability to coordinate across multiple stakeholders, teams, and geographies without losing momentum.
Real care for customers. You think about their experience constantly and push the team to get the details right.
Strong communication with both front-end and back-end engineers.
Experience taking problems (rather than strict guidelines) and developing strong solutions.
The ability to recognise what needs to be done, and just as importantly, what doesn't need to be done right now.
A talent for spinning many plates and context switching between competing demands without dropping quality.
Confidence in making decisions quickly, even with incomplete information.
Confidence tackling large-scale, ambiguous tasks and breaking them into something shippable.
An empathetic approach to collaboration.
Love for being the glue that holds cross-functional teams together.

Experience working on apps serving multiple markets or languages.
Familiarity with energy, utilities, or other regulated industries.

Who is Heidi?
Heidi is building an AI Care Partner that supports clinicians every step of the way, from documentation to delivery of care.
We exist to double healthcare’s capacity while keeping care deeply human. In 18 months, Heidi has returned more than 18 million hours to clinicians and supported over 73 million patient visits. Today, more than two million patient visits each week are powered by Heidi across 116 countries and over 110 languages.
Founded by clinicians, Heidi brings together clinicians, engineers, designers, scientists, creatives, and mathematicians, working with a shared purpose: to strengthen the human connection at the heart of healthcare.
Backed by nearly $100 million in total funding, Heidi is expanding across the USA, UK, Canada, and Europe, partnering with major health systems including the NHS, Beth Israel Lahey Health, MaineGeneral, and Monash Health, among others.
We move quickly where it matters and stay grounded in what’s proven, shaping healthcare’s next era. Ready for the challenge?

Heidi's core products are expanding in both scope and reach. Scribe already powers more than 3 million patient consultations a week, and Evidence and Remote are scaling behind it. We're now building out the New Bets function to create the next wave of new products.
This is a zero-to-one product role inside a company that already has proven impact and partnerships with the NHS, which is the combination every early-stage PM wants and almost never gets. Most v1s launch into silence.

Yours go in front of clinicians who already open Heidi every day, and who will tell you within a week whether you've built something they need. You can ship on a Tuesday, watch a GP use it on a Thursday, and know where you stand by Friday.

In addition to the external feedback loop, within the London Office, we have Clinicians sat within Customer Success, Regulatory Compliance and GTM, so there is plenty of lived experience within reach.
You'll own new bets end to end, not features on someone else's roadmap. You take a problem space from conviction to evidence: frame it, size the prize, prototype it, put it in front of real clinicians, and make the call. A few bets become Heidi's next product line. Most don't. Killing them cleanly, quickly and without ceremony is as much the craft as scaling the winners.
A small dedicated squad sits alongside you to build and test. If it needs a pilot scoped with a health system, you scope it. If it needs a landing page, you write it.
You might already be a PM. You might be a strategy consultant who is tired of recommending and wants to own what happens next. You might have run operations and spent the last two years fixing the product from the outside. The title matters less than the pattern: you build things, you move fast, and ambiguity makes you sharper, not slower.

Own each bet end to end: the problem it goes after, why it matters now, and the goals and success metrics you set and are held accountable to
Take each bet from thesis to evidence - frame the problem, size the prize and define what "working" means before anything gets built
Prototype fast, often yourself: a v0 built in Cursor or Claude Code beats a sprint of engineering time spent on the wrong thing
Get out of the building: sit in clinics, watch how visits actually run and turn what you see into the next sprint
Design pilots with commercial and regional teams that produce a decision. Think real accounts, real usage, honest numbers
Make the scale-or-kill call and own the narrative with founders, leadership and customers
Do whatever the bet needs: pricing, positioning, onboarding, the launch email. There's no one else to hand it to, which is the point
Graduate the winners into staffed product lines with roadmaps someone else can run, then start again

Form Health is a virtual obesity medicine clinic delivering physician-led, evidence-based care for obesity and related cardiometabolic conditions. Obesity affects more than 40% of U.S. adults, and as GLP-1 medications reshape the field, Obesity and Cardiometabolic Medicine is in a period of rapid growth and opportunity. Form Health is at the forefront of that shift, building a clinical model that combines rigorous, personalized medical care with the technology to make it accessible at scale.
Every Form Health patient works closely with a dedicated multidisciplinary Care Team, including board-certified physicians (many ABOM-certified, and endocrinologists), advanced practice providers, and Registered Dietitians who together deliver comprehensive, one-on-one treatment that includes nutrition, behavioral health, physical activity, and FDA-approved medication, if appropriate.

Through our mobile app, patients engage in regular video visits along with text messaging, photo journaling, and personalized educational content. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of clinical care and to treating every individual with empathy and respect.
Founded in 2019, Form Health is a venture-backed, mission-driven company partnering with leading employers and health plans to expand access to high-quality, guideline-based obesity and cardiometabolic care nationwide. We're deeply invested in our core value of putting patients first, and equally committed to building a culture where every employee is valued and we learn and grow together.

The Care Delivery team builds the tools that let our clinical team run a high-performing virtual practice — from prescribing and prior authorizations to the day-to-day workflows clinicians rely on to do their best work with patients.

This role is highly visible within Form Health : the tools you ship directly shape how our clinical team practices and, downstream, how our patients experience care.

We're looking for someone who's genuinely energized by hard, regulated, multi-stakeholder problems — with clinical, patient, payer, and operational constraints — as well as someone who uses AI as a real part of supercharging their work, rather than a buzzword on a resume.
This role will report to our Lead Product Manager for Care Delivery, with significant ownership from day one and plenty of room to help shape how the practice scales as the team grows. This role is fully remote and can be located anywhere in the U.S. ( Note: while not required, it is beneficial to be in or close to the Eastern Time zone given frequent collaboration with our Boston-based clinical and operations leaders)

Description
All organizations need security testing for their software and we are building the world’s largest and smartest pentest management platform to help solve this challenge at scale.
As a Contract Senior Staff Product Manager , you will drive the definition, delivery, and adoption of new product features and ecosystem integrations. You will be responsible for taking the lead of our next gen deliverables, from user discovery and roadmap prioritization to go-to-market execution - ensuring that our platform evolves to solve the most pressing challenges in the security workflow.
This is a full-time contractor position providing hourly coverage from October through the end of February . In this role, you will merge attention to detail with the ability to understand and align business objectives, while working collaboratively with cross-functional teams to drive customer insights and inputs directly into the development process. You will work closely with our other Customer Experience and Pentester Experience teams.
What You Would Do
As a member of a growing team of product managers your responsibilities include:
Rapidly acquire new technical knowledge while maintaining meticulous attention to detail. Champion the strategic product direction across the organization, ensuring internal and external synchronization while serving as a subject matter expert on industry developments and defensive security operations.
Represent our customers. Work with Product Design, Product Marketing, Sales and Customer Success teams to bring the customer’s voice into the development process.
Manage the platform next-gent feature deliverables . Make tough tactical prioritization decisions while enabling the company to think long-term.
Collaborate across teams. We win or lose as a team. Product managers are a critical role in creating alignment between engineering teams and stakeholders.
Have familiarity with information security, security operations, vulnerability disclosure, vulnerability management and other security domain areas.
Become an expert in pentesting best practices. You are ready to discuss and demonstrate product details with developers, product designers, security operations, pentesters, customers and sales prospects.
Measure success. Own the measures used to define success for your product. Success measures must be defined at the inception of a product and tracked throughout its lifecycle. Make measures visible to all stakeholders and interpret them into actionable conclusions and new hypotheses.
Lead Go-to-Market (GTM) Readiness: Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success to orchestrate successful feature launches. Develop launch strategies, create internal training materials, and support the creation of customer-facing collateral to ensure seamless adoption.
Maintain technical fluency in the operational workflows of modern cybersecurity tools, including vulnerability management or offensive security platforms. Evaluate how these tools function within a customer’s security environment to inform product development.

8+ years experience in Product Management and 3+ years experience in cybersecurity tools (vulnerability management or offensive security platforms), with a demonstrated ability to discover new opportunities and then define and deliver products. Experience in fast-growing software companies is a plus.
Strong technical skills - you can work alongside customers to help debug and improve our integration offerings.
Strong customer and stakeholder empathy. You must not only be the voice of the customer but at various times the voice of marketing, finance, engineering, sales and customer success. You must be able to channel many points of view.
Strong written and verbal communication skills. You’re great at explaining highly technical topics to technical and non-technical audiences, with a talent for building empathy for user problems.
Strong analytical capabilities is a plus.
Strong bias for action, creative thinking, innovation and data-driven product decision-making.
A can-do attitude and ability to juggle multiple priorities simultaneously.
Experience with agile software development.
Experience working with global team members (This team is a global team).
Hands-on experience with core cybersecurity tooling (e.g., DAST/SAST scanners, vulnerability management systems, or pentest workflow platforms). Articulate how security teams utilize these tools to identify, prioritize, and remediate risk, understanding the "why" behind the tooling workflow beyond simple API integrations.
Strong technical and product communication skills: Ability to translate complex security concepts into clear documentation, user guides, and release notes tailored to both technical developers and business stakeholders.
Full-time availability for the duration of the contract. You must be able to commit to full-time hourly coverage from October through the end of February, with no planned extended absences or vacations during the contract period (excluding recognized company holiday’s).

TL;DR Full-time. Berlin-based. No remote option available for this role. You sit with the PM.
Join GlassDollar as an Associate Product Owner and own the space between a good idea and a shipped feature.
Someone has to decide what "done" means, write it down clearly enough that an engineer can start on Monday, and stay close enough to the build that the scope does not quietly grow on the way. That is the job. You own it end to end: specs, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and a backlog that keeps everyone honest about what is actually shipping. Nobody hands you a ticket queue you did not write yourself.
The problem you'll be solving A corporation with 100,000 employees has thousands of expensive operational problems, and somewhere out there a startup has already solved most of them. Getting those two facts to meet is slow, political, and mostly attempted in spreadsheets that die in someone's downloads folder.
GlassDollar OS is the venture clienting platform that makes it repeatable: sourcing the startups, matching them to real problems, running the pilots, and rolling out what works across the whole organisation. Enterprise customers run real innovation budgets through it. What you scope this month decides what they can do next quarter.

s.h: What we´re looking for You have personally written the tickets.
s.t:
3+ years in a product company, where scoping and ticket-writing were actually your job rather than something you handed off.
You are technical enough to argue with engineers.
AI models, API contracts, estimates, sequencing. You push back with reasons, and you change your mind when the reasons coming back are better.
You can write.
A spec is a piece of writing. We will ask for a sample where the reasoning is visible, polish second.
You write specs worth acting on.
The valuable ones pull three threads together: where the product is going, what clients are actually telling us, and the knowledge already sitting in the team. You gather all three before you write, so what lands on the board is specific enough to build and pointed enough to matter.
You know what looks good.
You have a great sense of design and what feels good for users. We will ask you to build a prototype with AI and illustrate the specs visually.
You have worked somewhere small enough that there was nowhere to hide.
No layers between you and the consequences of a bad spec.
You want to be coached hard.
Direct feedback, weekly, on your actual work. You will scope alongside the product lead until you are doing it alone, and the goal is that this happens fast.
You are fluent with AI tooling, day to day.
We want to see the workflow, not hear it described.
You want the scope to grow.
The people who do best here end up owning areas outright: the major initiatives, the roadmap arguments, and the questions everyone else brings their doubts to. That is earned, and it is genuinely available.
What you`ll do Your job: turn validated opportunities into work an engineer can start on Monday.
Turning opportunities into scoped, sequenced, estimable work: specs, acceptance criteria, edge cases, dependencies
Running the backlog: grooming, prioritisation input, keeping the board honest about what is in flight, blocked, or quietly drifting
Being the interface between customer signal (support threads, CS conversations, call notes) and the engineering queue
Coordinating releases and checking that what shipped matches what was scoped
Presenting product decisions to varied stakeholder groups, from engineers to enterprise clients

s.h: What you'll be scoping over your first year
s.t:
Deep integrations into our customers' organisations. Their systems, their data, their identity stack. This is the work that turns GlassDollar from a tool people visit into infrastructure they run on.
Public REST APIs and MCP servers , so our customers' engineers and their AI agents can build on top of us.
AI embedded across the product , inside the surfaces people already work in.
Workflow automation inside the platform , so the work that used to take six meetings and a shared spreadsheet runs itself.
You will need to understand each of these well enough to write the spec and defend it in the room.
This is a doing role rather than a people-management one. Mid-to-senior individual contributor.
Requirements 3+ years in a product company, where you personally wrote the tickets
Technical enough to understand a data model, an API contract, and estimation
Demonstrable writing ability, be ready to share a spec, PRD or decision doc

Notion fluency

Help is in our first name! We show up for each other — not out of obligation, but because we’re invested in the team’s collective success. We share knowledge freely, lead with generosity, and practice empathy with our teammates, customers, and community.
Craft over Convention
Our success relies on the quality and craft of the work we put into the world. The status quo simply won’t work. So we insist on narrow focus, sweating every detail, and relentless pursuit of customer delight.
Progress not Perfection
Achieving our true potential — collectively and individually — requires constant progress and forward momentum. By creating a culture of curiosity and openness, we aim to create a safe space for mistakes, the ability to identify them quickly, and use them to get better.
Own the Outcome
Own the outcome means taking full responsibility for the results of your work, decisions, and contributions. It reflects a mindset of accountability, proactiveness, and follow-through. If you “own the outcome,” you don’t just complete tasks, you ensure your work leads to meaningful results, and take initiative to solve problems rather than passing them along.

Who is Boulevard?
Boulevard provides the first and only client experience platform for appointment-based, self-care businesses. We empower our customers to give their clients more of the magical moments that matter most.
Before launching in 2016, our founders spent months interviewing salon managers and working behind front desks to understand their pain points so we could design a modern, user-friendly platform that meets the unique needs of their business.

Our roots may be in hair salons, but we are built for the broader self-care industry, including many types of salons, spas, medspa, barbershops, and more. Our technology not only helps our customers survive but thrive. Take a look at how we (and YOU) can make that happen .
We have an insatiable curiosity and embrace experimentation. We believe that simple solutions require the most sophistication, and we design each and every detail to maximize potential, power, and impact. Do our values match? Read through our story and what we value the most .
Our team values and celebrates our diverse backgrounds. Being open about who we are and what we do allows us to do the best work of our lives. We believe in equal opportunity for all, and you should too.
Come do the best work of your life at Boulevard. Boulevard is the client experience platform purpose-built for salons, spas, medspas, and wellness businesses. More than 5,000 businesses use Boulevard — processing over $5 billion in payments annually. We've raised $188M in funding and are scaling fast, with growing ambitions in enterprise and multi-location operators.
Every salon, spa, and medspa deserves a front desk that never misses a call, never drops a message, and always knows what to say. Boulevard's AI Receptionist is building that — agentic AI that handles client communication across voice and text so businesses can grow faster, operate leaner, and deliver an exceptional experience every time. This role owns that vision end-to-end.

Own the AI Receptionist product end-to-end
You'll set the vision, roadmap, and success criteria for Boulevard's AI Receptionist suite — our answer to the modern contact center for self-care businesses. That means owning how AI engages clients in 1:1 interactions across voice and text: when it handles conversations autonomously, when it hands off to staff, and how that transition feels invisible to the client and effortless for the team.
Define what great AI-powered client communication looks like
You'll develop a deep point of view on where AI should handle interactions autonomously, where it should hand off to staff, and how to make that transition seamless — including how conversations maintain continuity across channels, how fallback behaviors are designed when AI can't resolve something, and how the overall experience feels coherent whether a client is talking to AI or a human.
Drive adoption and outcomes
You'll own the business outcomes for the AI Receptionist — revenue, adoption, and retention — and define the product metrics that drive them: autonomous resolution rate, agent productivity, CSAT, and more. You'll collaborate on pricing strategy and be expected to connect what's happening in the product to what it means for their business.
Represent the customer
You'll develop genuine fluency with how self-care businesses manage client communication today — what they trust, what they fear, what they'd delegate in a heartbeat and what they'd never let out of human hands. That customer insight is what separates AI that gets adopted from AI that gets turned off.

You'll be the bridge between our customers, our engineers, and our platform — turning real-world integration needs into a roadmap that makes Cosuno the infrastructure the construction industry plugs into.

The AI orchestration of your wildest imagination.
n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact.
Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve:
Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders
Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects
Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation
That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register .
We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.
Your main goal will be to make n8n's Core Platform ready for the company's next stage of growth: more scalable, reliable, secure, and flexible as customer usage and technical complexity increase. You'll own the foundations that everything else, including our AI and agent capabilities, is built on.

s.h: OWN THE CORE PLATFORM STRATEGY & ROADMAP
s.t:
Define and communicate the product strategy and roadmap for the Core Platform in partnership with Engineering and Product leadership.
Prioritize foundational investments based on customer impact, enterprise needs, technical risk, and engineering effort, and make trade-offs between near-term customer needs, technical debt, and long-term architecture explicit.
Lead product discovery for technically complex problems, engaging directly with enterprise customers and internal customer-facing teams.

Drive work on the scalability and reliability of n8n's execution engine, including areas like worker pools and distributed execution.
Improve the reliability of triggers and execution behaviour across complex deployment setups, from multi-main Cloud environments to self-hosted enterprise installations.
Shape a more secure and flexible approach to executing code within n8n.

Drive the planning and release of major or breaking platform versions, including migration strategy, stakeholder communication, and risk management.
Establish clear success measures and keep the squad accountable for outcomes, not only delivery.
Act as the bridge between the Core team and the wider org: Product, Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and Support, making platform trade-offs legible without oversimplifying them.
Treat internal product teams as customers of the platform: proactively mine their roadmaps for implicit platform requirements and turn cross-cutting needs into explicit Core Platform work before they become blockers.

Must-haves
Platform product experience: You have 5+ years in Product, with at least 2 to 3 years on platform, infrastructure, developer-facing, or backend/API products.
Technical depth: You're credible with senior engineers. You can reason about distributed systems, execution models, and reliability/scalability trade-offs, and hold your own in an architecture discussion. You're at home with non-functional requirements, where the details are the product.
Complex delivery track record: You've led cross-team technical initiatives with real delivery risk, ideally including a migration or breaking change.
Prioritization under ambiguity: You make trade-offs explicit and connect foundational or technical-debt work to customer and commercial outcomes.
Ownership and autonomy: You grab problems without being asked, fix what you see broken, and drive outcomes without waiting for direction.
Exceptional communication: You make complex platform topics understandable for technical and non-technical audiences alike.
Enterprise platform reality: You understand what running software in customer-controlled environments means, including self-hosted, air-gapped, and restricted deployments
Nice-to-haves
Hands-on ability: You can read code or prototype, even if you're not shipping it.
Enterprise exposure: You've worked with B2B SaaS requirements like security, compliance, or deployment complexity.
Security partnership: You're comfortable working with security teams on code execution, isolation, or compliance topics.
Domain familiarity: You know workflow automation, orchestration, or open-source / developer-community products.
Writing culture: You default to writing things down to create clarity and alignment.

Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery.

No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve.
Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals .

Hims & Hers is at an inflection point. We've built dozens of categories that people love, and we're great at the treatments themselves. But today those are dozens of separate, transactional relationships.

The opportunity in front of us is to invert that: to move from point solutions to one deepening relationship with each customer, where we understand them holistically across all of their concerns, help them navigate what to do, and let the individual treatments become secondary to the relationship itself.
That shift is what this role owns. It's a true 0-to-1 build, but not a cold start. You'll define a brand-new, relationship-first product experience that spans our existing categories and the new ones we create to support it, with everything we've already built as your foundation.

Picture a concierge-style experience for the person who knows they don't feel their best, wants to feel better, and is looking for a trusted guide rather than another one-off transaction: lab testing, continuous care, and access to treatment, wrapped into one experience that compounds over time.
This is a rare seat. We're a company known for physical product and transactional care, making the leap to a sticky, engagement-driven, relationship-driven digital experience. Few established companies reach that moment, and fewer put a single person at the center of it. You'll work across the entire company to define what it looks like, and you'll do it on top of the AI infrastructure we're building, as someone who works that way themselves.

Own the end-to-end consumer experience for this new relationship-first offering, from discovery and onboarding through ongoing engagement
Define the synthesis layer across our existing categories, and stand up the new product lines the offering needs
Partner with engineering and design to build AI into the core of the consumer experience
Partner with our clinical teams so protocols, safety, and education are core to the product experience
Shape short- and long-term roadmaps, driving long-term scalability while balancing day-to-day improvements
Operate with focus in a fast-growing, constantly evolving environment, where there are always more opportunities than resources

6+ years of product management experience, working collaboratively across cross-functional teams
A track record of building and shipping consumer products that customers love and that drive meaningful business impact
A strong, specific point of view on where AI can meaningfully reshape the consumer healthcare experience, and the excitement to build it into the core of the product
Fluency with AI agents and AI-native workflows. AI-native is your default operating mode: you work with agents the way most PMs work with docs, fluently and constantly
Strategic and tactical range: you can set the vision and also design and execute scalable processes from scratch, ideally in an operations-intensive environment
Strong communication and a low-ego, high-EQ style. You build alignment, partner well across functions, and bring people with you. This is a fully remote role, so clear written communication and proactive collaboration matter
Bonus: experience in health, wellness, or category-defining 0-to-1 products

The Company
Medely is a high-growth series-C technology start-up reimagining the future of healthcare work by providing an on-demand marketplace and workforce management tools. With the support of top-tier investors, Medely has quickly become a go-to platform for healthcare professionals to instantly access high-paying jobs with the freedom and flexibility to work when and where they want.
As a fully remote team of sharp, collaborative, and entrepreneurial individuals, we are dedicated to redefining the way healthcare workers and facilities work together to provide for patients. We are looking for passionate and skilled professionals to join our team and help us take on tough challenges in this fast-expanding healthcare industry segment.
Join us in our mission to transform the healthcare staffing industry and improve patient lives!
Own the Marketplace Powering Healthcare Work
Healthcare facilities need a faster, smarter, and more reliable way to connect with the clinical professionals who keep care moving.
That’s what Medely is building.
Our Flex marketplace is the core of our business today, connecting healthcare facilities with qualified professionals across the country. It’s proven, scaled, and business-critical. Now we’re focused on what comes next: improving how facilities engage, how professionals find the right opportunities, how matching works, and how we drive deeper retention and expansion.
We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager who wants real ownership of those problems.
This is not a “take tickets and ship features” PM role. You’ll work across complex marketplace dynamics - supply and demand, matching, trust, conversion, and retention - and be expected to challenge assumptions, define the right problems, and make thoughtful tradeoffs that drive measurable outcomes.
Why Now?
You’ll join at a point where the marketplace has real traction, real data, and real business impact - with meaningful room to shape what comes next.
You’ll have direct access to leadership, strong cross-functional partners, and ownership of product decisions that affect both the healthcare facilities we serve and the professionals who power them.
What You'll Own
Define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for key areas of the Flex marketplace
Own major product initiatives from discovery through launch and iteration, including high-quality PRDs, clear success criteria, and cross-functional alignment
Use product data, marketplace signals, customer insights, and user research to identify the highest-value problems to solve
Make strategic tradeoffs across conversion, retention, supply and demand, matching quality, operational efficiency, and user experience
Partner deeply with Engineering and Design while driving alignment across Product Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Clinical, Finance, and leadership
Measure what ships, learn from outcomes, and feed those insights back into product strategy
Identify risks, gaps, and opportunities before they become obvious - and bring a point of view on what we should do next
Apply AI and LLMs pragmatically as a force multiplier - both to simplify user workflows and to supercharge your own team's operational velocity

You want ownership, not hand-holding.
You’re comfortable turning complex systems, messy user behavior, and business-critical tradeoffs into intuitive, elegant user experiences. You can zoom out to understand marketplace dynamics and zoom in to define the workflow, metric, requirement, or edge case that determines whether something succeeds.
You’re analytical, highly accountable, and willing to challenge the direction when the evidence points somewhere better. You don’t just move work forward - you make the work sharper.
